subject: SLA questionnaire: measurement windows, partial outage crediting & latency buckets
messages:
From: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@globex.com>

Cc: procurement@globex.com

Subject: SLA questionnaire: clarifications needed on credits & measurement

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for filing the SLA appendix with the RFP — procurement and our platform team reviewed it and have a few clarifying questions before we include it in our bid evaluation:

1) Service credit calc: can you provide the precise monthly calculation for partial outages (i.e., region-only impact vs global)? We saw the table in the appendix but would like the arithmetic example for a 99.95 target.

2) Measurement window: do you measure availability over calendar months, rolling 30-day windows, or another approach? We need to know so our SREs can reconcile with internal monitoring.

3) Scheduled maintenance: what’s your exclusion policy (advance notice, typical window per quarter/month)?

4) Latency buckets: can you commit to p50/p95/p99 per-route and clarify whether errors/429s are included in percentiles? Also, is the percentile computed across all regions aggregated or by region?

5) Evidence: for disputes we require sample telemetry queries and example logs (request id, timestamp, response_time_ms, error code). Can you attach an example extract?

We're hoping for a consolidated reply we can attach to the RFP. Tom (cc) is our lead platform architect and will likely have a couple follow-ups.

Thanks —
Sarah
Sarah Lim
Head of Cloud Procurement
Globex Corporation

Subject: Re: SLA questionnaire: clarifications needed on credits & measurement

Hi Sarah (and Tom),

Appreciate the detailed list — below are concise answers followed by attachments with worked examples and sample queries. I'm summarising key points first, then adding the exact SLA wording we propose for your RFP.

Summary (high level):
- Uptime target: 99.95% (per-account, per-region) measured on a rolling 30-day window.
- Credits: monthly service credit tiers (pro-rata) with an arithmetic example attached. Region-only incidents are attributed to that region; global impact is only when >50% of capacity across regions is affected.
- Measurement: availability is calculated from successful serve-rate of production ingress (success=true) per logical route. Percentiles (p50/p95/p99) for latency are computed over successful requests only; error/429s are tracked separately for availability metrics.
- Scheduled maintenance: standard exclusion up to 8 hours/month (advance notice >=72 hours for planned windows). Extended maintenance is handled via SOW or enterprise calendar and is excluded if notified 14+ days in advance.
- Evidence: attached sample logs and a query we run against our observability store. We also included a CSV example of how credits would be computed for a sample month.

Attached: Redwood_SLA_Appendix_C_measurement_playbook.pdf (walkthrough + arithmetic examples), draft-MAP-Redwood-Globex.xlsx (mutual action plan + credit calculation sample), evidence-sample-logs.tar.gz (redacted sample logs).

Proposed RFP SLA wording (drop-in):
"Availability commitment: Redwood Inference will provide >= 99.95% availability measured per-account, per-region on a rolling 30-day window. Availability is defined as the percentage of successful requests (status code 2xx) measured at the platform ingress for production routes pinned to the customer's account. Requests returning 5xx/4xx (including 429) are considered unsuccessful and contribute to availability calculations. For latency commitments, Redwood provides per-route percentile targets computed over successful requests only. Maintenance windows (scheduled and notified per contract) up to eight (8) hours per calendar month are excluded from availability calculations. Service credits are applied per the schedule in Appendix C and are calculated on a monthly pro-rata basis."

Telemetry example (we run this exact query against our metrics store to produce the official numbers):
select
  percentile(response_time_ms, 50) as p50_ms,
  percentile(response_time_ms, 95) as p95_ms,
  percentile(response_time_ms, 99) as p99_ms,
  sum(case when success = false then 1 else 0 end) as failed_requests,
  count(*) as total_requests
from request_logs
where account_id = 'GLOBEX-ACCT-001'
  and route = '/api/v1/generate'
  and region = 'us-west-2'
  and timestamp >= now() - 30d;

We will provide the raw CSV extract (redacted request ids) for up to a 30-day window to support a dispute. For evidence chains we keep the original request id, ingress timestamp, backend response time, model id, and error code.

Next steps: if this aligns, we can append the drop-in SLA text to the draft contract and kick off a short MAP to align maintenance windows and run a final reconciliation exercise. I added Laura and Dev to help with the MAP items.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer

Redwood Inference

Karthik/Laura —

Thanks for the quick turn. Couple of technical follow-ups from our platform team:

- Latency percentile definition: you say percentiles are computed on successful requests only. Can you confirm that retries issued by client-side SDKs (that receive transient 5xx) are excluded from the percentile calculation if they eventually succeed? We need to make sure retries don't mask tail latency.

- Aggregation: do you compute p95 per-minute and then roll that up across the 30-day window, or compute percentiles across the full request set across 30d? The former can hide burst tail behavior.

- Sampling: what's the sampling policy under heavy load? If you sample 1/10th of requests for metrics, how do you ensure p99 accuracy?

If you have a short internal doc we can share with our SREs (even a one-pager) that explains the telemetry fidelity, that would be ideal.

--Tom
Tom Nguyen
Platform Architect, Globex

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fw: SLA questionnaire: clarifications needed on credits & measurement (internal)

Karthik/Dev — internal note to confirm our RFP wording and telemetry commitments before I send the MAP:

Proposed clarifications to respond to Tom:
- Retries: define percentiles over first-terminal-attempt per logical request (we log client_retry_id and attempt_number). Percentile calculation excludes client retries where attempt_number > 1 to avoid masking initial tail behavior.
- Aggregation: compute percentiles over the raw request set for the full rolling 30-day window (not minute-then-aggregate). This gives accurate tail numbers at the cost of larger compute; we already run this for enterprise accounts.
- Sampling: sampling is disabled for accounts with SLA commitments above 99.9%. For accounts on shared capacity we sample at 1/20 under extreme load but we bias-sample (higher probability for >95th ms buckets) to preserve tail fidelity. We'll include the sampling algorithm note in Appendix C.

I updated draft-MAP with these items (see tab 'telemetry_notes') and added a column for whether the account needs non-sampled telemetry (we mark Globex as 'true' by default).

-L
Laura Bennett
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Following internal alignment, here are the consolidated, definitive answers you can attach to the RFP. We've also attached the redacted CSV extract and the MAP. Please let us know if you'd like a short walk-through session (we can schedule a 30m call) to go over the query outputs and the credit calculation example.

Consolidated answers (final):
1) Availability and credits
  - Commitment: 99.95% per-account, per-region (rolling 30-day window).
  - Region attribution: incidents impacting < 50% of our regional capacity are scoped to that region. An incident is classified as 'global' only when >50% of total global capacity for the customer's pinned model family is affected.
  - Credit calculation: monthly pro-rata. Example in Appendix C: if availability for the 30-day window is 99.50% (0.45% below target), the credit is X% of that month's invoice (worked sample in attached spreadsheet).

2) Measurement windows and computation
  - Rolling 30-day window is the canonical measurement. We compute percentiles across the raw, unbinned request set for the window (no minute-level bucketing for final percentiles).
  - Percentiles (p50/p95/p99) are computed on successful requests only (first-terminal-attempt). Retries where attempt_number > 1 are excluded from percentile calculations to avoid masking initial tail events.
  - Sampling policy: for enterprise SLA customers (including Globex) sampling is disabled by default. For shared capacity customers we use an adaptive sampler biased toward tail events; details in Appendix C.

3) Scheduled maintenance
  - Standard exclusion: up to eight (8) hours per calendar month with >=72 hours notice. Extended/planned migrations require 14+ days notice and are handled via the MAP.

4) Evidence and dispute process
  - We'll provide a CSV extract containing: request_id (redacted), timestamp, region, route, response_time_ms, success, error_code. We retain the full trace for 90 days.
  - Disputes: open a support ticket with the sample window; we provide the platform extract and a reconciliation report within 5 business days.

5) Latency commitments (example drop-in text)
  - Per-route latency targets (computed over successful requests, rolling 30-day):
    * p50 < 120 ms
    * p95 < 450 ms
    * p99 < 950 ms
  - These are per-route, per-region. We can offer tighter targets on dedicated capacity or with pinned model quantization profiles.

Attachments included: Redwood_SLA_Appendix_C_measurement_playbook.pdf, draft-MAP-Redwood-Globex.xlsx, evidence-sample-logs.tar.gz.
